def factor_signed_path_efficiency_tail_balance(df):
    """Measure persistent directional movement with bounded attenuation for downside-shock fragility."""
    df_copy = df.copy()
    close = df_copy["close"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
    net_move = close - close.shift(126)
    path_length = close.diff().abs().rolling(126, min_periods=126).sum()
    efficiency = net_move / path_length.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    recent_move = close - close.shift(63)
    recent_path = close.diff().abs().rolling(63, min_periods=63).sum()
    recent_efficiency = recent_move / recent_path.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    ret = close / close.shift(1) - 1.0
    downside_pressure = (-ret.clip(upper=0.0)).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
    upside_pressure = ret.clip(lower=0.0).rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean()
    baseline = ret.abs().rolling(20, min_periods=20).mean().clip(lower=1e-6)
    fragility = ((downside_pressure - upside_pressure) / baseline).clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)
    signal = efficiency * recent_efficiency.abs() * (1.0 - 0.25 * fragility)
    df_copy["factor_signed_path_efficiency_tail_balance"] = signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    return df_copy["factor_signed_path_efficiency_tail_balance"]
rationale: The payoff-first parent supplies the primary signed long-horizon path-efficiency mechanism and its slower 63-bar directional confirmation, preserving persistent-trend exposure and low-turnover behavior. The secondary parent contributes one lightweight modifier: bounded downside-shock fragility attenuation based on recent downside versus upside pressure. This targets predictive instability in fragile downside regimes without averaging mechanisms or reversing the continuous raw signal.
